title: Nf Maxorder Om
objective: Implement P4 Ore-MacLane type trees, higher Newton polygons, quotient bases, MaxMin triangularization, certificates, and selector metrics in strict Python

handoff.summary: Implements an executable, fail-closed first-order p-regular OM slice in strict Python: immutable MacLane/Newton/residual type evidence, quotient numerators, generic exhaustively checked MaxMin, independently certified triangular bases, shared OrderBasis/LocalOrderResult mapping, selector metrics, frozen Sage/PARI-family fixtures, and a CPython/Sage.js benchmark. Complete scaled Eisenstein fixtures x^2-8, x^3-16, and x^4-32 have local index valuations 1, 3, and 6; x^2-12 stops at the repeated residual factor.
risks: Nonlinear residue fields, higher representative refinement, and multi-branch quotient assembly intentionally return incomplete or unsupported results.
OM auto-selection remains disabled until the integration branch supplies broader Round-2/Round-4/PARI/Hecke differential evidence.
Dynamic Sage.js certificate checking is substantially slower than CPython at degree 16 and is a source-transparent native-compilation target.
next_steps: Add om_types.py and om_maxmin.py to pyrightconfig.json and the test to the shared node-test manifest.
Wire regular_local_basis into the shared selector only for complete validated results; preserve not-applicable fallback states.
Add FLINT residual-field factorization and higher representative refinement, then extend differential fixtures to multi-branch and deep-index corpora.
